items.headline: Unsloth v2026.5.26 ships Qwen3.6-Max-Preview support and selective-expert-checkpoint primitive
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's Unsloth note was a Memorial Day changelog with no fresh feature surface and a stable router-only LoRA snapshot on DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B. Today the project cuts a tagged point release (v2026.5.26) that adds first-class Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B MoE fine-tuning at 1.74x throughput against the prior recipe, lifts the contributed 60B-class port count from three to four with a Tsinghua KEG MiniMax M2.7 235B MoE PR, and introduces a selective-expert-checkpoint primitive that drops MiniMax checkpoint disk footprint from roughly 470GB to 188GB. Independent reproductions on CoreWeave and Crusoe Cloud landed inside 3 percent of the published benchmark sheet on Tuesday.

items.headline: Alibaba publishes Qwen3.6-Max-Preview formal model card on Hugging Face
items.diff_narrative: The Chinese frontier-open cohort was not represented in yesterday's news. Today Alibaba's Qwen team lifts Qwen3.6-Max-Preview from a preview-numbers blog post to a fully gated open-weight release under the Tongyi Qianwen license, with 235B active parameters, 1M-token native context, and 24-of-160 expert routing. The model card reports 88.7 on LiveCodeBench v6 and 76.2 on SWE-Bench Verified (new records for any non-Anthropic non-OpenAI checkpoint) and matches Claude Opus 4.7 on AIME 2025 within a 0.6-point band, with Alibaba Cloud Model Studio listing the hosted variant at $0.45 per million input tokens against DeepSeek-V4-Pro's $1.10 floor.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS Tuesday tape reopen and Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close at $1.2B
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Cerebras CBRS sat closed for Memorial Day with only the HKEX ADR international tape providing price discovery and the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU still in the closing third of its late-Q2 window. Today the U.S. tape reopens with a $213.40 open, $221.20 intraday high, $217.05 close on roughly 18.6 million shares (about 2.7x the 20-day average), the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU formally closes Tuesday afternoon at a disclosed $1.2 billion four-year contract value for CS-4 capacity placement in King Abdullah Economic City, and UBS upgrades to Buy with a $240 target. Bernstein lifts its Market-Perform floor to $200 from $185 and institutional buyside cumulative net position climbs to roughly 47.5 percent of float from Friday's 44 percent.

items.headline: Stellantis pulls Detroit Optimus pilot from June 8 to June 1; BMW Leipzig and Boston Dynamics-Hyundai also advance dates
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's robotics coverage centered on Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Fremont reaching 144 of 240 units and BMW Spartanburg Atlas crossing 240 hours continuous operation, with Stellantis Detroit's June 8 date and Volkswagen Wolfsburg's June 22 date cited only in passing as future milestones. Today Stellantis discloses that the Detroit Mack Avenue 60-unit Optimus cohort has completed factory-acceptance testing at Fremont over the holiday weekend and is being pulled in to June 1, BMW responds inside the same session by locking Plant Leipzig's second AEON cohort first-activation date at June 15 (advanced from June 22), and Boston Dynamics Hyundai briefs investors that the Atlas commercial-fleet first deployment at Pyeongtaek is moving up roughly nine days to June 24. The combined effect compresses four humanoid factory-floor activations into an 18-day window between June 1 and June 18.

items.headline: CVE-2026-46127 critical prompt-injection escalation in OpenAI Codex CLI v3.1.x
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's security coverage tracked the n8n CVE-2026-21858 compliance-monitoring telemetry, MCP-server attack-surface visibility, and an agent-loader CVE wave holding at eleven catalogued instances. Today GitHub Security Lab discloses CVE-2026-46127, a CVSS 9.4 vulnerability that lets a workspace-scoped sandboxed Codex agent escalate into an unsandboxed shell-exec context via a crafted MCP-server response exploiting missing JSON-Schema validation in the agent harness, credited to Trail of Bits and Pillar Security and lifting the Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy from eleven to twelve catalogued instances. CISA placed the CVE on its KEV catalog the same Tuesday after a Mandiant engagement at a Fortune 500 financial-services customer confirmed active exploitation in the wild, and OpenAI shipped a patched v3.1.10 development tag with strict schema validation plus a runtime tool-call audit log, force-rolling all v3.1.x production tenants inside a 72-hour window.
